subtopics.title: Origin of International Labour Day
subtopics.summary: International Labour Day, also called Workers Day or May Day, is observed every year on May 1 to honour the contribution of workers. Its origin is traced to the late 19th century labour movement in the United States, where workers demanded an eight-hour working day. A large 1886 demonstration in Chicago went out of hand, and the incident known as the Haymarket Affair marked the start of the day. In 1889, Socialist Parties in Europe decided to celebrate May 1 as International Labour Day.

subtopics.title: ILO objectives, standards and reports
subtopics.summary: The ILO pursues four stated objectives: promoting fundamental labour rights, creating greater opportunities for women and men, enhancing social protection, and strengthening social dialogue and tripartism. Its international labour standards are Conventions and Protocols, which are legally binding treaties, and Recommendations, which are non-binding guidelines. The ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, adopted in 1998, names focus areas such as freedom of association and abolition of child labour. The ILO also publishes key reports, including the Global Wage Report.

ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work: adopted in 1998, amended in 2022
Focus areas: freedom of association, elimination of forced labour, abolition of child labour, elimination of employment discrimination, safe and healthy working conditions
Fundamental conventions listed include Minimum Age (No. 138) and Freedom of Association (No. 87)
Key reports include World Employment and Social Outlook, Global Wage Report, World Social Protection Report and World of Work Report
